title: Dashboard KPI: a compareTo delta is drawn green whenever the number rises — no way to declare lower-is-better, so a slower turnaround reads as good news
body:
Filing gate: ① user-visible defect, measured in the browser on @objectstack 18.2.0 (hotclm legal workbench, zh-CN, as the head of legal).

**Symptom.** hotclm's 「平均审批周转」 KPI tile (average days from submission to approval, `compareTo: previousPeriod`, hotclm PR #168) shows **「↑ 23% 较上期」 in emerald** for a turnaround that got 23% longer, which is a worse result shown as good news. Every "lower is better" measure has the same problem: durations, overdue counts, open deviations, cost.

**Why.** The renderer colours `delta.direction === 'up'` emerald for every measure (`packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx` ~1325 in the objectui tree now under `ui/`). The spec has no key on the widget or measure to declare the polarity, for example `compareTo: { …, betterWhen: 'lower' }` or a measure-level `polarity`.

**Expected.** An author can declare that lower is better for a measure or a compareTo tile, and the delta is coloured accordingly: up is red, or neutral, for such a measure. Without a declaration, the default could be neutral rather than green.

**Business reason.** A KPI's colour is read before its number. A green arrow on a slowing approval process tells the head of legal the opposite of what happened.

**Consumer.** objectstack-ai/hotclm (legal workbench `approval_turnaround`). The tile already drops its own success colour. The delta colour is the platform's.

**Duplicate search.** objectstack issues, all states: "compareTo delta colour lower is better", "metric trend arrow polarity", "previousPeriod delta direction good bad". The only related one is #25970 (compareTo without a window, closed). No duplicate.
